final_content.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. (1) If $D_X$ is any dualizing complex on $X$, then (a) $X$ is Gorenstein iff $D_X$ is derived-invertible on $X$; (b) for every $x\in X$, the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Gorenstein iff its derived stalk $(D_X)_x$ is an invertible object of $D(\mathcal O_{X,x})$; and (c) the locus of Gorenstein points is an open Gorenstein subscheme. (2) If $X$ is Gorenstein, then the existence of *some* dualizing complex on $X$ is equivalent to the structure complex $\mathcal O_X[0]$ itself being dualizing. The equivalences refer to derived-invertibility, not mere invertibility of a chosen cohomology sheaf unless the complex is concentrated in one degree.
hypotheses: X locally Noetherian; dualizing D_X for part 1, X Gorenstein for part 2.
conclusions: Gorenstein iff dualizing complex invertible, with local and open-locus claims and O_X normalization.
